transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess I’ve just been feeling kind of wound up most of the day. It’s probably not a huge thing, but my body feels like it’s bracing for something, even when I’m just sitting at my computer or trying to relax after dinner. I thought maybe I should come in and ask if that’s… you know, something worth checking on.
Do you find yourself worrying more than usual about things like work, health, or other everyday concerns?

Yes… I mean, I try not to make a big deal of it, because everyone has things to keep track of, right? But my mind does seem to jump around a lot lately. I’ll think about my sister in Arecibo, then whether I missed something at the office, then my husband driving home, or church commitments, or bills.

It’s like I’m mentally preparing for problems that haven’t even happened. I don’t know if that counts as “more than usual,” but it does feel like I’m doing it a lot.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like restlessness, feeling easily fatigued, or muscle tension along with these anxious thoughts?

Yes, I think so… mostly that wound-up feeling. I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s like my body is tense or sort of bracing for something, even when nothing is happening. I notice it sitting at my computer, and then again when I’m trying to relax after dinner. It’s not terrible, but it’s there a lot of the day.
Do you find it hard to control or stop the worrying, even when you try to focus on something else?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I do try to stop it. I’ll tell myself, “Daniela, enough, just focus on this report,” and for a minute I can, but then one little thought turns into five more.

And then before I realize it, I’ve spent half an hour checking messages or replaying what could go wrong. I know that probably sounds a bit silly, because nothing has actually happened, but it can be hard to pull myself back.
Do these feelings of worry and tension make it hard for you to do things you need to do, like work or take care of personal matters?

A little, yes… I mean, I’m still doing what I need to do. I get my work done, I show up for my family, and I’m still involved at church, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart or anything.

But it does take me longer to finish reports than it used to, because I keep checking things over. And… I’ve noticed I double-check messages or details more than I probably need to. I’ve also had to apologize a few times for sounding short with people I care about, which I don’t like. So yes, I suppose it does get in the way somewhat.
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on quickly, maybe with symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or feeling like you can’t breathe?

I don’t think so… not in that sudden, intense way you’re describing. I mean, I do get keyed up and uncomfortable sometimes, but it feels more like it builds with the worrying rather than coming out of nowhere all at once.

I haven’t really had episodes where I felt like I couldn’t breathe or anything like that. At least, not that I would call that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever felt sudden and intense waves of fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes, maybe with symptoms like chest pain, dizziness, or feeling detached from yourself?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I can get very uncomfortable when I’m worried, but not like a sudden wave that peaks in a few minutes.

I haven’t noticed chest pain or dizziness, and I don’t think I’ve felt detached from myself. It’s more… just worry building up, if that makes sense. Is that helpful?
Have you ever felt like you were detached from yourself or things around you, as if you were watching yourself from outside or things felt unreal?

No… I don’t think I’ve had that. I mean, I might feel distracted or kind of in my head when I’m worrying, but not like I’m outside myself or that things around me aren’t real.

I hope I’m answering that the right way. It just doesn’t sound like something I’ve experienced.

Do you find yourself especially anxious about particular situations or events, like going out in public, being in crowded places, or facing certain responsibilities, or is your anxiety more about just everything in general?

It’s probably more… general, I guess. Not so much one specific thing like crowds or going out.

My mind just kind of moves from one concern to another—like my sister in Arecibo, or whether I missed something at the office, or my husband driving home. Then I’ll think about church commitments or bills, and I start trying to prepare for problems that haven’t even happened yet.

I know everybody worries, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it does jump around a lot. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you ever experienced numbness or tingling sensations in your hands, feet, or other parts of your body, especially when you're feeling anxious?

Not really, no. I can’t say I’ve noticed numbness or tingling in my hands or feet when I’m anxious.

Sometimes I might feel tense or keyed up, but the tingling part doesn’t really sound familiar. I hope that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, even when you're tired?

A little, yes… though I don’t want to make it sound dramatic. Most nights I do fall asleep eventually, but I’ll wake up around three or four and my mind just starts going—like about my sister’s next appointment, or some server issue at work.

And even if I technically got enough hours, I can start the morning feeling like I didn’t really rest. I’m not sure if that counts as trouble sleeping, but that’s what it’s been like.
Have you been feeling this way—worrying a lot and feeling tense—on most days for at least the past six months?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to exaggerate it, but it’s been about thirteen months now.

It really started after my sister in Arecibo began needing a lot more help from the family, and since then the worrying and tension have been there most days, I’d say. Is that the kind of timeframe you’re asking about?
